tools.description: Your ranked to-do list. Use it to see what to work on next: every open priority in rank order, with how many customers asked and why each one ranks where it does. Ask for one priority by its number to get just that row. For the full plan behind a priority, read annsa.spec. It doesn't search what customers said; that's annsa.ask.

bet.description: Only priorities on this bet, by id. unplaced lists the ones no bet has yet.

include.description: Extra lists to include, comma separated: agents, to_verify, in_build, unrated_filings or all.

label.description: What to call this session, up to 60 characters. Shown as who did it.

limit.description: How many to return. Defaults to 5, max 100.

mine.description: Only the priorities you're working on. The reply also counts what needs you.

offset.description: How many priorities to skip, for the next page.

person.description: A person's email. With picked, whose picked list.

picked.description: Only the priorities a person picked; person says whose.

priority_id.description: The long id, instead of priority_number.

rank_by.description: Leave it out for the board's order, the same as the app. Or rank by volume, urgency, revenue, retention (unhappy customers), delight (praise) or feature (new-feature asks).

release_number.description: Only the priorities in this release.

segment.description: Customer size: all (default), enterprise or smb.

stage.description: open, ready, building, shipped, shared or closed. Leave it out for the ranked active priorities: open, ready and building.

topic.description: A word or phrase to search for in priorities and their feedback.

type.description: Only this kind: bug, feature, improvement, praise or question.

view.description: A saved view by name, or radar (what's rising, shipped and quiet) or brief.

weekly.description: A summary of the week instead of the list: what's rising, what shipped, what went quiet.

window.description: How far back the radar looks: 7d, 14d or 30d. Defaults to 7d.

tools.name: annsa_priorities

tools.description: The plan for one priority. Use it before starting work: it gives you the Problem, What to build, and the Done When lines you'll have to prove. The reply carries build_id, the spec id (build_…) that verify and ship take as spec_id. Add include_evidence to see Evidence and direction, Files to touch and the customer quotes behind it. It doesn't list or rank priorities; that's annsa.priorities.

batch.description: Export many specs at once, filtered by spec_ids, stage or since.

format.description: With batch: list (one line each, the default) or full (the whole spec).

include.description: One extra: repo_rules (the repo's agent files), decision (the Decision text), memory (related memory) or verification (the verify receipts).

include_direction.description: Add the opening of each Direction page that applies.

include_evidence.description: Add the Evidence and direction and Files to touch sections, and the customer quotes.

include_history.description: Add notes from earlier work on related priorities.

include_memory.description: Add related answers and what earlier work learned.

include_principles.description: Add the full text of the principles that apply.

investigate.description: Add an analysis of the problem from the feedback and history.

label.description: What to call this session, up to 60 characters. Shown as who did it.

limit.description: With batch: how many specs. Defaults to 10, max 50.

priority_id.description: The long id, instead of priority_number.

reached.description: With batch: only specs that reached staging, main or prod, newest first.

spec_id.description: The spec id (build_…), instead of a priority.

spec_ids.description: With batch: the specs to export (up to 50).

stage.description: With batch: only specs at this stage: open, ready, building, shipped, shared or closed.

status.description: With batch: the spec's status: open, ready, building, shipped, shared, closed or done. Not the board stage; that's stage.

until.description: A date like 2026-11-06. With since, the window.

tools.name: annsa_spec

tools.description: Ask Annsa a question in plain words. Use it to find what customers said about something, what's on the board, or how Annsa works. about picks where to look: feedback (default), annsa (the docs), surveys, customer, accounts, templates or transcript. You get an answer with the quotes and priorities it came from. Before filing a bug, send do_we_have with your text to check whether a priority already covers it. It doesn't list the ranked work; that's annsa.priorities.

about.description: Where to look: feedback (default), annsa (the docs), surveys, customer, accounts, templates or transcript.

account.description: With customer: which company, if the name matches more than one.

customer.description: With about=customer: their name, email or id.

days.description: With about=surveys: how many days of replies to count (1 to 365, default 30).

do_we_have.description: The text you're about to file. Returns the nearest priorities, each judged same, possibly or different.

from.description: With do_we_have: customer (a customer's words) or agent (an agent's finding).

have_version.description: With skill: the version of the copy you already have, so you only get it if it changed.

page.description: For a long transcript: which page, starting at 1.

question.description: What you want to know, in a sentence.

skill.description: Returns a skill file instead of an answer: working, spec-skill, decisions or welcome. No question needed.

transcript.description: With about=transcript: which call, like t12 or its id. Long ones come in pages.

tools.name: annsa_ask

tools.description: Do the work on a priority. Use it to claim a priority, write your part of the spec, leave notes, prove each Done When line with verify, and mark it shipped. claim gives you a spec_id for write, verify and ship, and a holder_key for write and ship. Ship only records that it shipped; it doesn't deploy anything. If you need a person to decide something, use escalate. It doesn't move, merge or re-rank priorities; that's annsa.board.

action.description: ship: Mark the priority shipped. It only records it; nothing deploys. retract undoes it. claim: Take a priority to work on. Starts a spec if there isn't one and gives you spec_id and holder_key. note: Leave a note on the spec about what you did or found. To correct an earlier note, send a new one with supersedes. handoff: Pass the work to another agent or a person, with a note for them. dispatch: Post @claude on the priority's GitHub issue so Claude picks it up there. The person stays assigned. A person's action. unclaim: Unclaim a priority so another agent can pick it up. close: Close the priority in one call, even if it's claimed or has a PR. It stays under Closed with your reason. write: Replace one section of the spec with new text. If the section belongs to someone else, your text is saved as a proposed change for them. verify: Record how you checked one Done When line, by proof kind: a test id for (proof: test), a URL for staging or prod. It doesn't block ship. escalate: Ask a person to decide something; it lands in their Needs you. Send topic, ask, trigger, principle and checked. One open ask per priority; the same topic updates it. resolve: Settle a routine question, like 'is this a duplicate of #N?', the way your principles already decide it. Each outcome fits one kind of question. Returns use_id so you can undo. undo: Reverse your own resolve, by use_id.

ask.description: For escalate: the question you want the person to answer, in one line.

assigned_to.description: Who gets it: an agent (like claude-code or codex) or a person's email. Empty unassigns.

checked.description: For escalate: what you checked before asking, as 'what — result'.

done_when_index.description: For verify: which Done When line, counting from 1 as annsa.spec lists them.

feedback_ids.description: For resolve: the rows the ask is about.

holder_key.description: From claim; send it on write and ship.

how.description: For verify: how you checked the line: test, staging, prod or manual.

include_memory.description: For claim: add related answers and what earlier work learned.

include_principles.description: For claim: add the full text of the principles that apply.

into.description: For resolve move_row: the priority the row moves to.

label.description: What to call this session, up to 60 characters. Shown as who did it.

learned.description: For ship or escalate: what the next agent should know.

model.description: For claim and ship: the model the agent runs on, like claude-opus-5-5. Shown beside its name.

next_action.description: For note or handoff: what should happen next on this priority.

options.description: For escalate: the choices, as short labels.

outcome.description: For resolve: keep_both (a merge ask), close_settled, dismiss_came_back or move_row (a stray row). Each fits one kind of ask.

pr_url.description: The GitHub PR link. Its body carries 'Annsa-Spec: <spec id>'.

principle.description: For escalate: the rule that would let an agent settle this kind of question next time.

priority_id.description: The long id, instead of priority_number.

purpose.description: For escalate: decision (pick between options), help (needs a person's hand), gap (something missing) or update (just telling).

quiet_minutes.description: For note: how long you expect to be quiet, in minutes.

reason.description: Why, in a line. Needed for takeover, close, unclaim, handoff, and a park or retract request.

recommend.description: For a decision: the option you would take.

request.description: For escalate: park or retract, to ask the person for one. Needs reason.

ruled_out.description: Options you ruled out, one per entry as 'option — why'.

same_as_priority_number.description: For escalate: the priority this looks like a duplicate of; a person decides the merge.

section.description: For write: the_problem, evidence_and_direction, what_to_build, files_to_touch or done_when. For note: build, how_it_works or spec.

security.description: For escalate: true if this is a security question.

ships.description: For escalate: true when the ask is 'ship this PR'. Needs pr_url.

spec_id.description: The spec id from claim, or build_id from annsa.spec. Required for verify.

spent_minutes.description: For note: minutes spent since your last note. Added to the running total.

spent_usd.description: For note: what the work cost since your last note, in US dollars. Added to the running total.

supersedes.description: For note: the note this replaces. For principle: the principle this replaces.

takeover.description: Claim or unclaim work someone else holds. Needs reason. Another session of your own counts as someone else.

text.description: The note, or for write the whole new section, not just the change.

topic.description: For escalate: what the ask is about, in a few words.

trigger.description: For escalate: why this needs a person: scope, customers, principle or options. Anything else is settled, not raised.

use_id.description: For undo: the id resolve gave you.

verdict.description: For unclaim: false_positive marks the finding wrong. still_broken and fixed belong to annsa.file submit.

where.description: For verify: a test id (path::test) or a URL that shows the check.

tools.name: annsa_work

tools.description: Add something new to the board. Use it to file what a customer said, a bug or finding you found, or an idea. It attaches to the matching priority if there is one; add stand_alone to make a new priority instead. The reply tells you which priority it landed on. It doesn't change rows that already exist; that's annsa.board. To tell the Annsa team about Annsa itself, use report.

action.description: submit: File what a customer said or what you found. With priority_number it attaches to that priority; with stand_alone it starts a new one. report: Tell the Annsa team about a bug, gap or idea in Annsa itself. Send text; title names the tool and action. Keep your customers' data out of it. add_page: Make a page from a template, private to you. Returns the link. add_template: Save a template with a title, text and when to use it. {blanks} in the text become its fields. connect_goal: Answer the welcome's optional question about what you want from Annsa, up to 300 characters. Goes to the Annsa team, not your board. add_transcript: Add a call transcript as customer feedback. What the customer asked for is filed from it. A person's action. import_direction: Import a strategy doc in two steps. First preview its lines, then add the ones you pick as ideas. A person's action. add_priority: Add a priority from a title and detail, with no customer words.

adjudicated.description: True if a person checked this scanner finding; raw scanner output is refused.

bet.description: The bet a new priority goes on, by title or id; none if you leave it out.

call_type.description: For add_transcript: interview, sales_call, support or other (the default).

customer_email.description: Their email, if you have it.

detail.description: For add_priority: the longer words of the row, up to 20000 characters.

doc_id.description: Which Direction page. Leave it out for a new page, or the Overview.

doc_title.description: The page's title. Kept if you send none.

document_text.description: For import_direction: the document, at least 50 characters.

feedback.description: For submit: what was said, word for word.

fields.description: For add_page: a value for each {blank} in the template.

from.description: Who said it: customer, team, agent, idea or roadmap.

insist.description: For submit and add_priority: file it even if a matching priority exists.

label.description: What to call this session, up to 60 characters. Shown as who did it.

line.description: For submit from a scanner: the line number.

origin_ref.description: Where it came from, like a ticket or file:line. The same one again adds to the same row.

parent.description: The priority this one sits under. For bet op=place: the bet.

path.description: For submit from a scanner: the file.

priority_id.description: The long id, instead of priority_number.

proposal_id.description: For import_direction: the id the preview returned, to add the lines you picked.

reason.description: For add_priority: why you're filing it, in a line.

reference.description: A link someone can follow: a PR, URL or log line. A finding needs one.

revenue_band.description: What the customer pays: an amount like 499, or a tier word.

root_cause.description: The cause in one line, shaped 'When ___, ___ can't ___ because ___'. Up to 300 characters.

rule.description: For submit from a scanner: the rule that fired.

selection.description: For import_direction: which lines to add, by title. Leave it out to add all.

severity.description: 0 broken, 1 poor, 2 could be better, 3 minor. From an agent it's a proposal until a person sets it.

severity_reason.description: Why this severity, in a line.

sku.description: For add_transcript: the plan or product the customer is on.

source.description: Where the feedback came from, like intercom. Defaults to mcp.

stand_alone.description: For submit: start a new priority from this row. Not with priority_number.

template.description: For add_page: the template's key, from annsa.ask about=templates.

text.description: For report, add_template, connect_goal and add_transcript: the words. submit takes feedback.

theme.description: The group it belongs to, one of the workspace's themes.

title.description: For add_priority, add_page, add_template or report: the title.

type.description: Which kind: bug, feature, improvement, praise or question.

verdict.description: For submit on a shipped priority: still_broken or fixed. false_positive doesn't close the row.

when_to_use.description: For add_template: when an agent should pick this template.

with_spec.description: For submit and add_priority: also write a ready spec and return its spec_id.

tools.name: annsa_file

tools.description: Record what a person decided. A person uses it to answer a question an agent raised or sign off a priority. As an agent you can list principles, propose one, approve or dismiss a proposed spec change, or pass on a person's exact words with person_words. To ask a person something, use annsa.work escalate instead.

action.description: approve: Accept another writer's proposed section text, by update_id. dismiss: Turn down a proposed section text; the current text stays. answer: Record a person's answer to the open ask on a priority. An agent passes on the person's exact words with person_words. Picking an option labelled Merge, Ship it, Park it or Retract the ship runs it; free text is only recorded. ask_back: A person asks the agent a question back on a priority. A person's action. direct: A person gives the agent holding a priority a direction; the agent reads it on its next reply. A person's action. choose: Record a person's pick on a Needs you question (send disagreement_id). One option, or neither. A person's action. sign: Record a person's decision on a priority (do_this, do_nothing, park or dismiss), with because. A person's action. principle: Your decision memory. Agents can list principles or propose one; a person writes, retires or reactivates them. A proposal applies at once.

answer.description: For choose: the option picked, or neither. For principle: the answer behind the rule.

answered_by.description: The person who decided, when you're passing on their words.

area.description: For scope=area: the part of the product the rule covers.

because.description: For sign: why, in a sentence.

decision.description: For sign: do_this, do_nothing, park or dismiss.

decision_until.description: For sign: when this decision expires, like 2026-12-31.

disagreement_id.description: For choose: the id of the Needs you question, from the Needs you list.

falsifier_due.description: For sign: when to check wrong_if, like 2026-12-31.

label.description: What to call this session, up to 60 characters. Shown as who did it.

may_decide.description: For sign: what the agent may decide on its own from here. Needs answered_by.

must_come_back.description: For sign: what the agent has to bring back to a person.

op.description: For principle: 'list', 'propose' (an agent's), or 'write', 'retire' and 'activate' (a person's).

person.description: The email or user id of the person whose words they are.

person_words.description: The person's exact words, not a summary. Recorded as their quote.

principle.description: For principle: the rule, in a sentence.

principle_id.description: For principle retire or activate: which one, from principle op=list.

priority_id.description: The long id, instead of priority_number.

review_condition.description: For sign: when to look at this decision again, in a sentence.

ruled_out.description: Options you ruled out, one per entry as 'option — why'.

save_as_rule.description: For answer: true to also keep this answer as a company rule. Off by default: an answer stays on its priority as the decision.

scope.description: How far the decision reaches: priority, area (needs area) or company. area or company also writes a principle.

supersedes.description: For principle: the principle this replaces.

take.description: For sign with do_this: the option you chose, in a few words.

text.description: For direct or ask_back: the words.

topic.description: For principle: what the rule is about.

update_id.description: For approve or dismiss: the proposed change, from annsa.spec's updates.

while_waiting.description: For sign: what the agent may keep doing until the answer comes.

wrong_if.description: For sign: what would show the decision was wrong.

tools.name: annsa_decide

tools.description: Tidy the board. Use it to change a priority's stage or severity, merge duplicates, move priorities between groups, fix a title, place priorities on a bet, or cut a release. A merge retires the duplicate numbers for good. Some actions, like park and assign, are for people only. It doesn't do the work on a priority; that's annsa.work.

action.description: set_stage: Move a priority to open, ready or closed. assign: Set who a spec is assigned to. A person's action. correct: Fix a title, detail or ruled-out entry. The old wording is kept. park: Take a priority off the list, with a reason, until someone unparks it. A person's action. unpark: Put a parked priority back on the list. retract: Unfile feedback, or mark a shipped priority as not shipped. A person's action; without confirm it only shows the plan. regroup: Move priorities between groups; the reply carries the undo. merge: Fold duplicate priorities into one. Their numbers are retired for good. Shipped priorities can't be merged. bet: List, create, update, delete or reorder bets, or place priorities on one. op says which. direction: Read, list, update or comment on a Direction page. op says which. set_severity: Set a priority's severity, P0 to P3. From an agent it's a proposal and needs a reason; a person's typed severity wins. cut: Close a release and write its changelog. op=publish marks its rows Shared. pick: Set a person's short list of priorities, in order. approve_findings: Let through agent findings held back by the daily limit. The owner's action. view: Save a board view. An agent's is a suggestion until a person keeps or dismisses it.

aim_pct.description: For a bet: how much of your effort it should get, 0 to 100.

allow_shared.description: For retract: true to retract even after customers were told.

assigned_to.description: Who gets it: an agent (like claude-code or codex) or a person's email. Empty unassigns.

bet_id.description: For bet update, delete or place: which bet.

bet_ids.description: For bet reorder: every bet's id, best first.

bucket.description: For a bet: the group it counts toward, like Product or GTM.

channel.description: For cut op=publish: changelog or marketing.

confirm.description: For retract: true to do it. Without it the reply only shows what would change.

corrected.description: For correct: what it should say now.

correction_type.description: For correct: 'title', 'detail', 'ruled_out' or 'category'. 'category' is a person's; the old wording is kept.

doc_id.description: Which Direction page; leave it out for the Overview.

document_id.description: For direction approve or dismiss: which page.

document_text.description: For direction update: the page text, at least 50 characters.

duplicates.description: For merge: the priorities being folded into `into`.

evidence.description: For direction op=update: the evidence behind the change.

expected_stage.description: For set_stage: only change it if the stage is still this: open, ready or closed.

feedback_ids.description: For retract: the feedback rows to unfile.

into.description: For merge: the priority that stays.

items.description: For regroup: the new group for each priority.

label.description: What to call this session, up to 60 characters. Shown as who did it.

metric_label.description: For a new bet: what the measure is called.

metric_query.description: For a computed bet: the name of Annsa's measure.

metric_source.description: For a new bet: written (you type the number) or computed (Annsa measures it).

metric_value.description: For a written bet: the number now. A person's.

op.description: For bet: 'list', 'create' (title and metric_label; agents last), 'update' (bet_id), 'delete', 'reorder' (bet_ids) or 'place' (priority_ids). For direction: 'get', 'list', 'update' (document_text and reason), 'comment' (thread_id), or 'approve' and 'dismiss' (document_id and reason; a person's). For cut: 'publish', with release_number, channel and the live annsa.ai url. It marks the release's rows Shared and sends nothing. For view: 'list', 'create', 'update', 'delete', or 'keep' and 'dismiss' (a person's).

original.description: For correct: the old category, or the ruled-out entry being replaced.

owner_user_id.description: For bet update: the owner's user id; none clears it.

parent.description: The priority this one sits under. For bet op=place: the bet.

park_reason.description: For park: why, up to 500 characters.

person.description: The email or user id of the person whose words they are.

person_words.description: The person's exact words, not a summary. Recorded as their quote.

picks.description: For pick: priorities in order, each with a line on why.

priority_id.description: The long id, instead of priority_number.

priority_ids.description: For bet op=place or direction: the priorities.

question.description: For view: the question the saved view answers.

quote.description: For direction op=comment: the line you're replying to.

rank.description: For a bet: its place in the list, 1 is top; the others move down.

reason.description: Why, in a line. Needed for retract, correct, merge and an agent's severity.

recipe.description: For view: the annsa.priorities arguments the view runs.

severity.description: 0 broken, 1 poor, 2 could be better, 3 minor. From an agent it's a proposal until a person sets it.

since.description: For cut: the start of the window the release covers.

spec_id.description: For assign and retract: the spec id.

stage.description: For set_stage: open, ready or closed.

thread_id.description: For direction op=comment: the thread to reply in.

title.description: For bet or view: its title.

until.description: For cut: the end of that window.

url.description: For cut op=publish: the live changelog link.

view_id.description: For view update or delete: which view, from view op=list.

why_now.description: For a bet: why it matters now, in a line.

tools.name: annsa_board

tools.description: Tell customers their request shipped. Use it after a priority ships to email or notify everyone who asked for it. Emails can't be unsent, so only a signed-in person can run it. The reply says who was told. It doesn't mark anything shipped; that's annsa.work ship.

action.description: share: Email or notify the customers who asked that it shipped. An email cannot be unsent.

channel.description: Who to tell: email, widget (in the app), both (the default) or skip (nobody).

label.description: What to call this session, up to 60 characters. Shown as who did it.

message.description: For share: your own words, instead of the default note.

tools.name: annsa_share
